name: Shobach
source_summary: The commander of the Aramean king Hadadezer's army, who led a coalition of Aramean forces against David at Helam and was killed there when Israel won a decisive victory.
family_friendly_summary: Shobach was the commander of the army of Hadadezer, a king of Aram (Syria) who fought against King David. After the Ammonites insulted David's messengers and started a war, they hired Hadadezer's Aramean soldiers to help them fight Israel. Shobach gathered the Aramean troops and led them into battle against David at a place called Helam. David personally led the Israelite army out to meet them, and Israel won a decisive victory. Shobach himself was wounded and killed in the fighting. His defeat ended Aram's willingness to help the Ammonites, and the surrounding kings made peace with Israel instead.
adult_story: Shobach (also spelled Shophach) was the commander of the army of Hadadezer, the Aramean king of Zobah, during the war Israel fought against the allied forces of Ammon and Aram in David's reign. After the Ammonites provoked war by humiliating David's envoys, they hired Aramean mercenary forces to reinforce them; when those forces were routed by Joab, Hadadezer summoned additional Arameans from beyond the Euphrates under Shobach's command to make a second attempt against Israel (2 Samuel 10:6-16; 1 Chronicles 19:16). This time David himself crossed the Jordan and led Israel's army directly against the assembled Arameans at Helam. The battle went decisively to Israel: David's forces killed the drivers of seven hundred Aramean chariots and forty thousand horsemen, and Shobach the commander was struck down in the fighting and died there (2 Samuel 10:17-18; 1 Chronicles 19:18). His death broke Aram's will to keep fighting for Ammon -- the vassal kings who had served Hadadezer made peace with Israel and became subject to David instead (2 Samuel 10:19). Shobach's brief, violent appearance in the text marks a turning point in David's wars: a formidable foreign general defeated, and a coalition against Israel dissolved, under the LORD's hand of victory for His anointed king.
